newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia bonds disappointed on rates, data a lift.
newsitem.headline: Australia bonds disappointed on rates, data a lift.

text.p: *Australian bonds rise off their lows after retail trade and building approvals data, but remain in negative territory and well below their early highs after RBA stayed silent on rates.
*Moody's says credit rating outlook for Australia improving

Australian bonds were in negative territory after a rocky morning that saw them rally early, only to weaken on RBA's silence on a rate cut, before being lifted off their lows by retail trade and building approvals data.

In between, Moody's Investor Service issued a statement saying the credit rating outlook for Australia was improving, citing the steady fiscal policy framework and the RBA's prudent monetary policy stance.
Bonds had initially rallied strongly ahead of the 9.30 a.m. announcement time of any rate cut, but had already begun to weaken when the time passed and the RBA stayed silent.
"An interesting morning," one short end trader said. "Lots of excitement with the RBA doing nothing and the data releases."
Bonds continued to weaken after 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT), with even the announcement of the positive outlook by Moody's not enough to turn sentiment around.
"It had a monetary impact on the bond market, but then they decided to sell anyway," one trader said.
The data released showed retail trade rose 2.9 percent in May, while building approvals were up 2.2 percent. While in line with expectations, these figures found favour with the market.
Bonds lifted off their lows on the data, which analysts said did not rule out another rate cut in the next month or so.

"I think (the reaction) is mainly because of the building approvals data. The fact that it did include the Olympics and it was probably weaker than people would have expected given that," Axiom Funds Management economist Matthew Drennan said. ---------------------(SPREADS)--------------------------- AUD VS 3-YR 10-YR * AUD 3-YR/10-YR SPREAD

The weakening of bonds through the morning sees spreads undo much of Tuesday's narrowing. With the short end more vulnerable to pull back on the rate cut disappointment, the curve flattens slightly. -------------------(TECHNICALS)-------------------------------- FUTURES *SUP-RES *2ND SUP-RES *3RD SUP-RES *RSI
